                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>

                        <goals>

            <plugin>

                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <configuration>
                    <argLine>@{argLine} -javaagent:${org.mockito:mockito-core:jar} -Xshare:off</argLine>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>

    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <parent>
        <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
        <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-parent</artifactId>
        <version>4.1.1</version>
        <relativePath/>

    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
    <artifactId>demo</artifactId>
    <version>0.0.1-SNAPSHOT</version>
    <name>demo</name>
    <description>Spring Boot demo project</description>

    <properties>
        <java.version>25</java.version>
    </properties>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter</artifactId>
        </dependency>

        <!-- JUnit Jupiter, Mockito, AssertJ, Hamcrest, Spring Test / Boot Test -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-test</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <!-- Exposes ${org.mockito:mockito-core:jar} so Mockito can be loaded as a Java agent -->
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-dependency-plugin</artifactId>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>properties</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>
            <!-- Register Mockito's inline mock maker as an agent instead of self-attaching (JEP 451) -->
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <configuration>
                    <argLine>@{argLine} -javaagent:${org.mockito:mockito-core:jar} -Xshare:off</argLine>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
                <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

I set up a Maven Spring Boot project in `/work` with mocking, assertions and Spring context loading for tests. `mvn test` passes: 4 tests, 0 failures, no warnings.

**Testing support:** one test dependency, `spring-boot-starter-test`, covers all three:
- **Mocking:** Mockito, plus `@MockitoBean` to swap a mock in for a real bean inside the Spring context.
- **Assertions:** AssertJ, with Hamcrest and JSONAssert included too.
- **Loading the Spring context:** `@SpringBootTest` and Spring's test support.
- **Test runner:** JUnit 5.

All versions come from Spring Boot, so you don't set any in `pom.xml`.

**Setup:**
- **`pom.xml`:** Spring Boot 4.1.1 (the newest stable release) and Java 25.
- **Mockito agent:** by default Mockito attaches itself to the running JVM, which prints a warning and won't be allowed in future JDKs. I configured the test plugin to load Mockito as a Java agent instead, which removes the warning.
- **Sample code:** `DemoApplication`, a small `GreetingService`, and the `GreetingRepository` it uses, so the tests have something to run against.
- **Other files:** `application.properties` and `.gitignore`.

**Example tests** in `src/test/java/com/example/demo/`, one per pattern:

| Test | Pattern |
|---|---|
| `GreetingServiceTest` | Plain unit test with Mockito, no Spring |
| `DemoApplicationTests` | Loads the full Spring context and checks real beans |
| `GreetingServiceMockitoBeanTests` | Loads the Spring context with one bean replaced by a mock |

The machine has JDK 26, which builds Java 25 code without issues. I haven't committed anything.
